meta.title: From intent to evidence
meta.subtitle: One prepared walkthrough. Seven accountable roles. Evidence with boundaries.
meta.status: Prepared walkthrough — not a live agent run
meta.footer: Illustrative policy. No client adoption claim.

acts: AI Has Accelerated Coding, Not Software Delivery
Reimagining the Lifecycle, From Code Generation to Confidence
The Four Capabilities of an Agentic SDLC
From Theory to Practice, One Change Travels Through the SDLC
Closing the Confidence Gaps, What Changed?

scenes.title: Faster coding is only the beginning.
scenes.lede: Follow one ordinary change from a vague request to an inspectable decision — then use what it teaches us to improve the next change.
scenes.takeaway: The bottleneck moves from producing code to agreeing intent, carrying it through and judging the result.
scenes.notes: Say: Nattu has established the lifecycle problem. Land: faster generation is useful, but it is not the same as dependable delivery.

scenes.title: The request is simple. The behaviour isn’t.
scenes.lede: Before implementation, expose the decisions hidden inside the sentence.
items: The owner, a support agent, or anyone with an order ID?
Before fulfilment starts, while it is in progress, or afterwards?
Does a repeated request return the same outcome or create new work?
What remains true if cancellation only partly completes?
scenes.takeaway: The first useful output is not code. It is a decision-ready set of questions.
scenes.notes: Show: select Capture & Refine, then open its role and skill files. Do: point to the separate domain context.

scenes.title: Turn the request into an agreement.
scenes.lede: A reusable method asks; product-specific knowledge constrains; a human decides.
items: Afterwards, refuse unchanged; returns outside scope.
Eligibility, repeats and failure states are explicit.
scenes.takeaway: Capture & Refine creates a shared, testable agreement — not merely a longer document.
scenes.notes: Prepared walkthrough. Do not describe this as a live autonomous run.

scenes.title: Separate what travels from what belongs here.
scenes.lede: The capability improves when reusable technique and product truth can change independently.
items: Permissions · validation · repeats · errors · partial failure
Order states · ownership · fulfilment · payment obligations
scenes.takeaway: The questions can travel across products. The business answers usually cannot.
scenes.notes: Show: expand the full skill, then the domain file. Land: domain truth remains human-owned.

scenes.title: Carry intent through six explicit decisions.
scenes.lede: The seven roles are a practical mapping onto the lifecycle — not a replacement for it.
items: Decide whether it can enter the codebase.
Decide whether users can safely receive it.
scenes.takeaway: Intent → Build → Prove → Merge → Release → Learn.
scenes.notes: Keep merge and release as separate decisions. Then move to Nattu’s four capabilities.

scenes.kicker: THE FOUR CAPABILITIES OF AN AGENTIC SDLC
scenes.title: Four capabilities make the lifecycle dependable.
scenes.lede: They reduce ambiguity, scale merge confidence, automate release confidence and govern decisions with clear authority.
items: Inspect current, relevant evidence for a merge decision.
Bound authority, approvals, provenance and learning.
scenes.takeaway: Capability connects faster production to confidence and control.
scenes.notes: Use these exact capability names. Do not rename them as the four journey chapters.

scenes.title: Design makes the behaviour visible before planning the build.
scenes.lede: The agreed requirement becomes states, interactions, edge cases and an experience contract.
scenes.takeaway: Design precedes planning so implementation is not forced to invent the user experience.
scenes.notes: Land the sequence explicitly: Capture & Refine → Design → Planner.

scenes.title: The plan names the path and the proof.
scenes.lede: Technical choices are tied to acceptance criteria, risks and verification before code changes.
scenes.takeaway: A plan is useful when the Builder and Tester can tell what done means.
scenes.notes: Show: role and skill source. Point out the explicit stop condition.

scenes.title: Build the bounded change — and preserve the agreement.
scenes.lede: Implementation and tests remain traceable to the decided behaviour and technical plan.
scenes.takeaway: The Builder does not silently resolve product ambiguity in code.
scenes.notes: Use the worked-example file if present; label all example artefacts as prepared.

scenes.title: Evidence answers a claim — not every possible question.
scenes.lede: Verification links observed results to the current change, environment and acceptance criteria.
items: Exercise happy, refusal, repeat and failure paths
scenes.takeaway: Not run is not passed. Old evidence does not prove the current change.
scenes.notes: Do not invent execution results. Open repository evidence only when present.

scenes.title: Why should we trust this change?
scenes.lede: Review brings intent, change, evidence and open concerns into one bounded decision. The NFR X-ray and merge score are aspirational here, not runnable proof.
items: Current evidence supports the scoped claim.
No conclusion: missing, unavailable or outside scope.
The evidence belongs to an older change or baseline.
scenes.takeaway: Leadership needs the basis for confidence — not a fabricated product score.
scenes.notes: Land: merge confidence is not release confidence. Do not imply an NFR X-ray or merge score was executed.

scenes.title: Ready to merge is not ready to release.
items: Scoped behaviour · review findings · relevant tests · known limitations
scenes.takeaway: A reviewed change is not a blanket guarantee about the production system.
scenes.notes: No product score is shown; no release claim is made.

scenes.title: One finding can improve three different things.
scenes.lede: Keep reusable capability, product knowledge and delivery work separate — then review each change.
scenes.takeaway: The loop closes only when learning changes a later decision or delivery outcome.
scenes.notes: Show: Curator source files. Land: version, review, maintain and recheck.

scenes.title: Scale the method — not uncontrolled access.
scenes.lede: Good output, permission to act and worthwhile economics are separate things to establish.
items: Permitted repositories and data · approved tools · traceable decisions
Credentials · permissions · production data · merge · release · deployment
scenes.takeaway: Permission to inspect a repository does not imply permission to deploy.
scenes.notes: No claim of enterprise adoption. This is an operating pattern for evaluation.

scenes.title: Adopt around one bottleneck, then inspect the result.
scenes.lede: Use a real feature, real owners and explicit evidence boundaries before expanding.
items: Named owners, permissions and approval gates.
Spend, human effort, elapsed time, quality and rework.
scenes.takeaway: The objective is a better accepted outcome — not the cheapest first answer.
scenes.notes: The free 90-minute masterclass refers to the overall event. This contribution’s working 50-minute slot remains provisional. Do not imply a human rehearsal occurred.

scenes.title: Start with one bottleneck. Improve the next change.
scenes.lede: The same request is now agreed, designed, planned, built, tested, reviewed and curated through accountable handoffs.
scenes.takeaway: Every feature can improve the product, the domain understanding and the capability used next time.
scenes.notes: Reset returns to the opening. Recovery: PDF and PPTX carry the same scene sequence offline.
